- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 70), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 1–2% to prevent overcorrection.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 18-day mean is 68–69, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5 points if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0 point in the 5–7 day window following sentiment change.
- In low-sentiment (0.00–0.33) periods, model tends to underestimate true price; add 0.5–1.0 point to forecast if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- Avoid forecasting below 65 when sentiment is above 0.33 — model often underestimates support levels; use 65 as floor unless sentiment is clearly bearish.
